TERM

  "notes": "The palm is one of the more stable biblical symbols. Two strands dominate and are usually blended: (1) the flourishing righteous (Psalm 92) and (2) victory/triumph (John 12; Revelation 7), the latter especially strong in Christian liturgy, iconography, and martyrology. There is no serious interpretive dispute over these core meanings; the alternatives listed are supplementary emphases rather than competing readings. The Hebrew word tamar also appears as a personal name (Genesis 38; 2 Samuel 13) and a place name (Tamar/Hazazon-tamar), which some studies fold into the symbolism but which mainstream interpretation treats separately."

BOOK ENTRY
The righteous — “The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree… planted in the house of the LORD” — carved beside the cherubim on the temple's walls and doors, and in the hands of the white-robed multitude before the throne. Its branches are kappot — bent palms, the frond named for the open palm of the hand (Leviticus 23:40).

BOOK'S COMMON-VIEW NOTE, IF PRESENT
(none)

SCRIPTURE REFERENCES PRINTED WITH THE ENTRY
(Ps 92:12-13; 1 Kings 6:29; Ezek 41:18; Lev 23:40; John 12:13; Rev 7:9)

AVAILABLE KJV EXCERPTS
Psalms 92:12 — The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree: he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
Psalms 92:13 — Those that be planted in the house of the LORD shall flourish in the courts of our God.
1 Kings 6:29 — And he carved all the walls of the house round about with carved figures of cherubims and palm trees and open flowers, within and without.
Ezekiel 41:18 — And it was made with cherubims and palm trees, so that a palm tree was between a cherub and a cherub; and every cherub had two faces;
Leviticus 23:40 — And ye shall take you on the first day the boughs of goodly trees, branches of palm trees, and the boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook; and ye shall rejoice before the LORD your God seven days.
John 12:13 — Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.
Revelation 7:9 — After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands;

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

First reduce both readings to their minimum core identifications. Do not let
extra detail create an artificial disagreement.

- MATCH: the core identifications are equivalent. Differences are merely
  wording or immaterial detail.
- REFINED: the book preserves the consensus's general referent or category but
  materially changes its extension, boundary, conditions, or precision. A
  narrowing may reject some cases the broader consensus admits; a broadening
  may admit cases it excludes. This is real disagreement at the boundary, but
  not replacement of the central referent.
- DIVERGENT: the cores materially contradict. Both claims cannot be true of the
  same referent in the same context and sense; accepting the book requires
  rejecting or replacing the consensus identification. A source and its
  product remain different referents when the book explicitly denies their
  identity, even if they are causally related.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus or listed alternative covers the book's
  core identification. Novelty is absence from consensus, not contradiction.

Use `core_relation` to expose the relationship at the center and
`extension_relation` to expose disagreement over the cases covered. A REFINED
verdict must state what cases the book adds, excludes, or reclassifies. A
DIVERGENT verdict must identify a replaced referent or material contradiction,
not merely a narrower boundary.

Treat the two axes independently. A core-divergent reading may still retain
some cases covered by the consensus while rejecting its central identification;
therefore DIVERGENT does not require disjoint extensions. Conversely, a
narrowed extension is REFINED only when the consensus's central referent or
category remains intact.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
